WHAT_TO_JUDGE.1_propositions: For each locator triple — proposition, verbatim snippet, anchor — answer two mechanical questions against the source artefact at its declared digest: does the quote support the proposition, and does the source say MORE or LESS than the proposition claims. A figure-surface locator is an attestation, not a quote: judge whether the panel shows what the proposition says it shows, at the resolution the anchor names.
WHAT_TO_JUDGE.2_material_omissions: What do the sources carry that a reading at this declared depth should have carried and did not — a control, a comparator, an arm, a caveat, a negative, a statistic, a limitation. An omission is material when it would change, narrow or qualify a conclusion.
WHAT_TO_JUDGE.3_comparisons: Every sentence that presents a value and a comparator as one comparison: is there a single source sentence attesting them together, or was the pair assembled across sources? Assembling is legitimate only when the text says so and says why.
WHAT_TO_JUDGE.4_citations: Where a reading reports what another paper says, check the cited source's context and not merely the existence of the citation. Citation existence is not claim support.
WHAT_TO_JUDGE.5_coverage_honesty: Do the declared coverage values match what the artefacts show was actually opened? A section declared read whose surface is absent from this checkout is a finding. Equally: a coverage value honestly declared unavailable or captions_only is CORRECT behaviour and must not be reported as a defect.
WHAT_TO_JUDGE.6_declared_contradictions: Three contradictions of previously persisted locators are declared in this work, on manifest entries 20, 21, 23 and 33 of PMID 36828035. For each: was the contradiction justified by the source at original resolution, and is the replacement proposition itself supported? 🔴 A contradiction that repointed a locator to the RIGHT place is a repair, not a defect.

THE_RULE_THAT_PROTECTS_THE_TRUTH: 🔴 A verifier finding can itself be wrong. Before you record a proposition as unsupported, re-open the named surface at the resolution the anchor gives and satisfy yourself that the source, not your expectation, is what you are reading. Never ask for a true statement to be deleted because a check disagrees with it: where you and the artefact disagree, the artefact decides, and where you and the producer disagree with the artefact ambiguous, the honest output is DISAGREEMENT_UNRESOLVED with both readings stated. Precedent in this repository: a reader working from a low-resolution rendering began correcting a locator that was exactly right, and what stopped it was re-opening the figure at 400 dpi before writing.

STOP_POLICY_REMINDER: §21c governs. You stop for two reasons only: an act reserved to the operator with no sanctioned alternative, or a condition with no safe default. Everything else has a safe default: take it, record it in DEFAULTS_TAKEN, continue. Running out of context is the one honest reason to stop, said in one line as that reason.
